text: Every child has a spark, but not every child gets the chance to show it. This is GranthAI. In Sanskrit, granth means a book, and its root means to tie together. That's what we do: we tie learning, people and opportunity together, around every child.

In Ireland, only fifty-four percent of children in care complete the Leaving Cert, against eighty-seven percent of all children. Teachers in DEIS schools do remarkable work, but one teacher can't sit beside twenty-five children every evening.
It starts with a profile. Aoife is nine. She picks what she loves: football, space and drawing. She chooses her language, her teacher confirms consent, and GranthAI starts learning how she learns.

Here's the difference. Aoife asks a general chatbot: what's three quarters plus a half? It hands her the full answer. She copies it, and learns nothing. In GranthAI, she tries first, and answers four sixths. GranthAI spots the exact mistake: she added the tops and the bottoms. So it shows her a picture, gives one hint at a time, and she finds five quarters herself.
Behind every reply, a Bayesian model tracks what she has mastered, what she's forgetting, and what to review next.

To keep her motivated, her feed follows her interests: why a football curves, a rocket to build this weekend, a book she'll love. Gentle check-ins let her share how she feels, and if something is wrong, GranthAI never keeps secrets. It connects her with a trusted adult at school.

Then it gets bigger. Our ranking and clustering algorithms find children with the same passions across different schools. Aoife and three pupils from two other DEIS schools form a space club, and build a project together.
Each group is matched with a vetted retired teacher as a mentor, by subject, availability and language. Children gain role models, and retired teachers gain meaningful, paid work.

Teachers get their time back. The class dashboard shows which misconceptions are spreading, suggests a ten-minute mini lesson, and flags who might need a quiet word. It even helps plan outdoor activities, because principals told us their pupils need safe places to play.
Future Me turns interests into real routes, from CAO courses to apprenticeships.
And it's safe by design: no ads, no selling data, no emotion detection, and built for GDPR and the EU AI Act.
GranthAI. Not another chatbot, but a whole team around every child. Starting in Ireland's DEIS schools, and growing across the UK and Europe.
